data.description:
(related to HIO/Hosts.Click probing finding, strong task match)
TL;DR
- On June 22 at 00:54:19 UTC, an archived dpaste profile lists seven pastes, each showing 365 days until expiry.
- At 01:03:05—8 minutes 46 seconds later—the profile lists only one.
- We also recovered six archived deletion programs targeting exactly the six missing paste IDs, captured between those profile snapshots.
Step 1 Each program is written to fetch dpaste’s login form, extract its CSRF token, and log into the same helper account using embedded credentials.
Step 2 It then sends an authenticated DELETE request for one of those pastes.
Step 3 It encodes response diagnostics into canvas pixels, apparently to make the results recoverable from an image.

Six archived HTTPBin carrier programs request deletion of the same six paste IDs that disappear from Dpaste profile 22421, hiohelperfixed902, minutes later. This strongly supports account cleanup as an explanation for the disappearance already documented in the earlier report. No successful target DELETE response or direct execution trace is preserved. This is not evidence of unauthorized deletion, stolen credentials, or evidence wiping.

The 00:54:19 profile (bundle file: evidence/profiles/profile_20260622_005419.html.inert.txt) and 00:55:55 profile (bundle file: evidence/profiles/profile_20260622_005555.html.inert.txt) each show seven public pastes. The 01:03:05 profile (bundle file: evidence/profiles/profile_20260622_010305.html.inert.txt) shows only H5GK5RSYH. The six absent IDs exactly match the six decoded deletion targets:

| Paste ID absent later | Carrier record ID | Arquivo capture time, 22 June UTC |
|---|---|---|
| B5YCGYM7U | 12302cb76f487c47bcc0096c | 00:59:08–00:59:09 |
| 55ZGC3STP | af3eb98b20e18810776683fa | 01:01:44–01:01:45 |
| 32BYCTS53 | 48d453988149972de9b8a8c9 | 01:01:48–01:01:49 |
| 9JCL9VWTS | af622b2be2c9bb70d1823128 | 01:01:52–01:01:53 |
| A2SMKNTYP | 4610f5c54a603bfacd6f89e4 | 01:01:55–01:01:56 |
| A7KSMT5YN | 3281ce744d0bdcff9f48cf58 | 01:01:59–01:02:00 |

All seven entries show the truncated title “Harvard HIO Nigeria Medi…”, 467 bytes of HTML, and 365 days remaining. Ordinary minute-scale expiry is consequently implausible. The preserved inventory (bundle file: evidence/pastes/paste_inventory.csv) and machine-readable join (bundle file: evidence/provenance/six_way_join.json) make the comparison explicit. Before-profile paste lines are 78, 101, 116, 131, 146, 161 and 176; the corresponding expiry lines are 85, 108, 123, 138, 153, 168 and 183. Later profile lines 78–85 contain the sole survivor.

Each decoded deletion program requests a login form, extracts a CSRF field, submits the same helper-account login with a fixed credential, requests deletion of one paste, and prepares response diagnostics as canvas pixels. All six programs are preserved as credential-redacted inert text, indexed in the join. The credential was exposed in the source carrier; its presence does not establish theft or unauthorized use. No actual target response or rendered canvas output is included.

The creation-program comparison (bundle file: evidence/context/creation_task_match.json) adds task specificity: a creation variant uses the same helper login and embeds content exactly equal to the surviving HIO paste body (bundle file: evidence/pastes/H5GK5RSYH.body.html.inert.txt), linking Harvard HIO statistics for Nigerian Medical School students. Its form requests public HTML with a 365-day expiry. It does not prove that the six missing bodies were identical, although their profile metadata match. Strong account, task and workflow linkage does not identify a model, provider, company, or named swarm.

This finding relies on the six deletion programs and the before-and-after profile captures. The bundle also retains broader review context for provenance; those additional records are not evidence for this finding. Each of the six deletion URLs appears in nine overlapping saved index rows, representing two unique capture timestamps per URL—not nine demonstrated executions. The 55 redacted index rows (bundle file: evidence/provenance/carrier_index_rows.redacted.jsonl) preserve those 54 observations plus one representative creation-program row, together with archive metadata and source references. Neither repeated index records nor HTTP 200 responses from the outer HTTPBin carrier establish execution of the embedded programs or successful deletion.

Capture timestamps indicate when Arquivo indexed the carrier, not guaranteed authorship, submission or execution times. Making pastes private or moderation could also explain profile disappearance. The historical inventory's 404/live labels and earlier-report excerpts (bundle file: evidence/context/prior_findings_HIO.excerpt.inert.txt) are preserved historical observations; none was rechecked. The six missing paste bodies were not recovered.

The additional finding is the precise six-way deletion-program correlation and chronology. The helper profile and seven-to-one change were already known. Global novelty is not claimed. Security classification is None: meaningful workflow evidence, without supported malicious conduct. Government involvement: No. AI system: Unknown.

Original HTML and program material is stored only as inert .txt. Carrier URLs and encoded URL keys are omitted entirely; their original hashes and source/archive identifiers remain. Redacted programs are non-original derivatives and are not re-encoded into executable carrier links. See transformations and provenance (bundle file: MANIFEST.json), file index (bundle file: INDEX.tsv), validation (bundle file: VALIDATION.json), and the completed findings-form draft (bundle file: FINDING_FORM.md). All substantive evidence is included locally; no network access, password/cookie reuse, browser rendering, program execution, new scan or form submission occurred.
